## v80 — Session 867 — Harness and packs: the pack mule, the draught horse and the yoked ox (backlog L3, prototype only)
Session 855's beasts of burden owed their harness and packs. What an animal wears is the bodies builder's; the wagons and carts they draw are props, and stay the look builder's. This adds two parts to `creatures.js` and three plans, `HARNESSED`. Each plan is a Session 855 animal with what it carries. It is prototype only, under FREEZE #297.

- **`packs`:** two panniers, one hanging either side of the spine, over a canvas blanket draped like the saddle's. Each has a leather lid band and a leather hanger strap down the flank. A strap runs across the back, and a bedroll is lashed on top behind the panniers. Everything sits outside the fur, as the saddle does, and is rigid on the spine bone.
- **`harness`:** placed at a point `at` along the neck's polyline and set square to the neck there, on that neck bone, so the head moves free of it.
  - A `collar` is a padded leather ring with two brass hames.
  - A `yoke` is a wooden beam across the top of the neck, overhanging by `over` each side, with a bow under the neck.
  - `fit` scales both to the flesh.
  - To place it, the neck now records its points, radii and squash (`B.neckPts`, `B.neckR`, `B.neckS`). Nothing reads them but the harness.
- **The plans:**
  - the pack mule, with packs at 0.55 of the spine;
  - the draught horse, at 1.1 times the horse, with its collar at the neck's root at a fit of 1.4, because the neck's flesh blends into the chest there;
  - the yoked ox, with its yoke at 0.7 of the neck, behind the horns.
  - Six gear tones (`blanket`, `pack`, `leather`, `roll`, `brass`, `wood`) are shared by all three.
### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`creatures.check.mjs`: all 873 checks pass** across 110 plans.
  - The three build in 0.37 to 0.41 s, with 31 or 32 bones and 34,784 to 38,236 triangles.
  - Their skin weights sum to one, and every foot reaches its target through every gait.
- **Pictures:** `creatures-packmule.jpg`, `creatures-draughthorse.jpg`, `creatures-yokedox.jpg` and `creatures-yokedox-front.jpg`. Three faults were found and fixed in turn:
  - The first collar sat inside the neck's flesh, and only a brass hame showed. It was moved to the polyline's root and fitted 1.4 times larger.
  - The first yoke sat at the shoulder, with its bow drawn as a dark band. It was moved forward behind the horns.
  - The yoke then floated a hand above the neck, so it was lowered to 0.82 of the neck's height.
  - The panniers were lowered so their tops sit below the back.
### Needs eyes
- **The panniers are plain boxes.** Wicker or sacking would want a texture and softer corners.
- **The collar** slopes back with the horse's neck, which is right. But it is thin where it meets the chest, and from the side it reads as a line.
- **The ox's bow** is mostly inside the thick neck, so the yoke reads as a beam alone.
- **Traces and reins** are not drawn. They run to the wagon, so they want the look builder's carts first.

## v80 — Session 874 — Loose hair that falls from the head, and no seam down the back of it (B1, Michael's note on #272, prototype only)
Michael kept the groomed hair on #272 with a note: some of the styles "aren't quite landing". The pictures showed which, and why. The loose style was the worst. Its strands walked down the skull to the nape, followed the neck in, then dropped as a straight curtain. From behind, the hair pinched to the width of the neck under the head, like a vase. Over the shoulders, the strands pushed out by the body stayed vertical and left stepped shelves. And every free style had a dark line of bare scalp down the back of the head. The parting sent every strand left or right of the midline by its side, so behind the crown the two halves pulled apart. This is still under FREEZE #297, so it touches only the prototypes (`people.js`, `builder.check.mjs`).

What changed in `buildHair`:
- **The parting is only at the front.** A strand rooted forward of the crown still goes to its side. Behind it, the side pull grows smoothly from nothing at the midline, in proportion to how far the root sits from it. So the back of the head is covered across the middle. This changes the short and loose styles. The gathered styles (the braid, the braids, the tail, the bun) already walked to their gathering point and draw the same strands as before.
- **Loose hair leaves the skull where it turns under.** It used to let go at a fixed height. Now a strand lets go where the surface under it starts to face down (its normal's y below −0.08), or 5 cm below a height drawn per strand, whichever comes first. From there it falls straight down, with a little spread to its side and never back in toward the head's axis. So it parts from the skull on a tangent and hangs as wide as the head.
- **What fell is smoothed.** Eight passes along the fallen part, then cleared off the body once more by the same rule the walk uses (its layer height on the head, the clothes' clearance below the neck). A first try cleared it by the clothes' 2 cm on the head as well, and that drew a ledge round the skull. The strand's normal also blends from the skull's to the hanging one over eight steps, so the light has no seam where it lets go.
- **Lengths vary more,** 0.7 to 1.15 of the style's length and a little shorter at the sides, so the ends are not cut on one line.
- **Under the fur mantle, loose hair goes inside the collar.** The mantle's eleven fur shells stand 10 cm off the neck. Hair laid over that came back out below in a tangle (it did before this session too, as a block hung off the fur). Two tries at lifting it over the collar failed the same way. So, as the hood already tucks the hair in, a loose strand under a mantle ends where the collar takes it.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 145 checks pass**, ten of them new. Every style but the two braids, with and without the mantle, is checked for **no bare seam down the back of the head**: points on the scalp's back midline above the occiput, with no strand over them within 4 mm.
  - Now 0 of 88 points for every checked style. Before this session it was short 18 of 88 (20.5%) and loose 7 of 88 (8%).
  - The two braids are not checked, because they part at the back as braids do (11% of the midline is bare).
- No strand is under the skin or on the face, in any style.
- The loose style is 244,408 triangles and builds in 2.0 s. With the mantle it is 192,290 triangles and 1.5 s, since the strands stop at the collar.
- The gathered styles build the strands they built before. A first version drew one more random number per strand for every style. That moved every root and put a stripe across the tail and the bun; the number is now drawn for loose hair only.
- **Pictures:** `builder-styles-back`, `-front` and `-mantle` were shot again. New: `builder-woman-loose.jpg` (from behind), `builder-woman-loose-side.jpg` and `builder-woman-loose-mantle.jpg`. `builder-woman-loose-before.jpg` is the same view on the old code.
### Needs eyes
- **The hairline** is still a hard edge, set high, and every style reads slicked back. The front of the scalp wants finer, shorter strands thinning out at the edge. That is the next refinement on #272's note, and with the brows ("still fugly"), the one that matters most at conversation distance.
- **Loose ends** are still visible cards at the hem: the tips taper, but each strand is one flat card. Clumping strands into locks near the ends would read softer.
- **Hair over the fur mantle**: the tuck is a choice, not a law. Hair worn out over the fur would need the fur's outer surface in the push-off map, as the cloak's map holds the skirt.

## v80 — Session 875 — A hairline that thins onto the brow (B1, Michael's note on #272, prototype only)
The second part of #272's note ("some of the hairstyles aren't quite landing"). Session 874's entry left the hairline owed. Seen from the front, every style started on a hard painted edge. The dark under-shell that keeps the scalp from showing through the strands was cut on one curve across the forehead, with ±2 mm of jitter. The strands rooted on that line were already full width. So each head wore a cap with a ruled brim. This is still under FREEZE #297, so it touches only the prototypes.

What changed in `people.js`:
- **The under-shell fades into the skin.** Over the forehead, the shell now runs from the skin's own colour at its edge to its full colour 1.4 cm in. The skin's colour reaches the shader as a uniform (`skinC`), so one program serves every person. The edge itself wanders with a low noise of ±4.5 mm, so the line is not one curve.
  - A first try thinned the shell by discarding a stipple of 0.9 mm cells. At conversation distance it read as pixel noise, so it was dropped for the colour fade.
- **Strands at the front edge are finer.** A strand rooted within 1.5 cm of the front hairline (measured on the rest body) has its card narrowed, smoothly, down to 0.35 of its width at the edge. Nothing new is drawn from the random stream, so every style keeps the strands it had.
- **Not changed:** the temples and the sides. There the edge is where the root region's triangles stop, not the shader's curve, and it is still a mesh edge.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 157 checks pass**, twelve of them new: every style, with and without the mantle, checks that **the hairline thins**.
  - Every style has 74 to 112 strands rooted within 0.75 cm of the front hairline.
  - Those edge strands are 0.43 to 0.44 of the width of the strands behind the band.
- The seam, skin and face checks of Session 874 all still pass. There are no page errors, which also covers the new shader.
- **Pictures:** `builder-woman-face.jpg`, `builder-man-face.jpg` and `builder-styles-front.jpg` were shot again. The old face pictures are kept as `builder-hairline-before-woman.jpg` and `builder-hairline-before-man.jpg`.
### Needs eyes
- **The temples** still end on the root region's mesh edge, which shows on the man as a step at the side of the brow. A fade there needs a distance to the region's border per vertex, not the forehead's curve.
- **The man's fade** reads a little like a receding hairline from straight on, since the colour fade starts at the shell's own edge. If it reads wrong in play, the fade could start 5 mm lower than the strands' roots.
- **Every style still reads slicked back.** The strands lie 3 to 14 mm off the scalp, which gives no lift at the crown. More height there is the next refinement, together with the brows.

## v80 — Session 876 — Brows combed up and out, finer and denser (B1, Michael's note on #272, prototype only)
The last part of Michael's note on #272: "eyebrows look pretty fugly still". Session 824 had already drawn each brow as a shape filled with short hairs lying on the skin. Close up, three faults remained:
- **An upright fan.** The hairs at the inner end, by the nose, were combed nearly straight up (on average 0.74 of vertical) and ran past the brow's top edge. Each brow started on a fan of spikes.
- **Too few, too coarse.** There were 700 to 900 hairs a face, each card 0.28 to 0.46 mm wide, so the brow read as a scribble of dark and light strokes.
- **A square start.** The inner end was cut square at the nose.

This is still under FREEZE #297, so it touches only the prototypes (`people.js`, `builder.check.mjs`).

What changed in `buildBrows`:
- **The head is combed up and out,** at about 50°, not near upright. A hair whose tip would pass the brow's upper edge by more than 0.8 mm is shortened to fit, down to a 1.5 mm minimum.
- **The head starts sparse.** Over the first tenth of the brow, a root is kept with a chance that rises from 0.3 at the nose, so the brow fades in rather than starting on a cut.
- **The hairs are finer and denser:**
  - 1.8 times as many hairs, 1,200 to 1,360 a face;
  - 0.20 to 0.34 mm wide, tapering to a fifth at the tip;
  - 3.5 to 8 mm long;
  - lying flatter (their tips 0.2 mm off the skin against 0.5);
  - each a shade from 0.93 to 1.07 of the brow's colour, so they read as hairs of one brow.
- **Their own random stream.** The brows draw from a stream of their own (`seed|brows`). The person's stream still moves on by the twelve numbers a hair that Session 824 took from it. The cloak is drawn after the brows from that stream, so every cloak folds exactly as before. The cloak checks read the same numbers as Session 839's: hems 13.0, 2.6 and 1.4 cm in, and folds 3.7, 4.7 and 5.5 cm deep.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 162 checks pass**, five of them new. On each of the five rolled genomes, the head's hairs are combed at 0.577 to 0.589 of vertical on average (Session 824's comb is about 0.74), and no hair passes the brow's top by more than 1.5 mm (0.9 to 1.1 mm).
- Every brow hair's root is on the skin (1,204 to 1,359 of as many), and the tips lie 0.2 mm off it.
- **Pictures:** the six `builder-brows-*.jpg` and the two face pictures were shot again. Session 824's brows are kept as `builder-brows-before-man.jpg` and `builder-brows-before-woman.jpg`.
### Needs eyes
- **Is this the brow Michael wanted?** His note gave no reference, so this is judged against real brows: a sparse head, a dense body and a thin tail. A thick, low Markish brow or a fine Aurennais arch is set by the people's ranges (`brow` thickness and arch, Session 826). That is the place to tune if a people's brows read wrong.
- **The skin under the brow** is still only 20% darker, by the body's vertex colours. The face's vertices are too far apart for a finer shade there.
- **Grey and white brows** for the old are not drawn. Brows take the hair's colour.

## v80 — Session 877 — Hair roots on the skin, and some lift for loose hair (B1, Michael's note on #272, prototype only)
Sessions 874 to 876 each left one owed item: every style read slicked back. Each strand of Session 804's hair kept one height over the scalp from root to end. Its root was put that far up as well, anywhere from 3 to 14 mm off the skin, so the strands at the hairline stood off the forehead. Over the crown, loose hair lay no deeper than a braid pulled tight. This is still under FREEZE #297, so it touches only the prototypes.

What changed in `buildHair`:
- **The root sits on the skin.** Every strand now starts 3 mm off the skin. It rises to its own layer height over its first 5 cm along a smooth step, so the hair builds depth back from the hairline. It does not start at full depth on it.
  - A first try started at 1.5 mm. That left 51 to 110 strand points a head under the skin where the scalp curves, so it went back to the old minimum of 3 mm.
  - A second try rose over 2.5 cm. From the front, that showed a rim at the hairline.
- **Loose hair stands deeper.** Its layers now reach 2.3 cm (up to 2 cm over the root height), where they reached 1.4 cm. Short hair now reaches 1.2 cm, from 0.9. The gathered styles keep theirs, since hair pulled into a braid, a tail or a bun lies tight to the head.
  - At 1.4 cm, loose hair stood 8.4 mm deep over the crown against a braid's 7.8 mm, too little to see. That is why the depth was raised.
- No random number is added, so every style keeps its strands.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 175 checks pass**, thirteen of them new:
  - **Every strand roots on the skin**, in every style with and without the mantle. The highest root is 3.2 to 3.4 mm off the skin; Session 804's reached 14 mm.
  - **Loose hair stands higher over the crown than a pulled-back braid**: 10.9 mm against 7.8 mm, as the mean height of the strand points above the head's middle.
- Every other hair check still passes: no seam, the hairline thins, and nothing is on the face. The braid, the tail, the bun and short hair each have one point under the skin, inside the 0.2% the check allows.
- Loose hair is 247,384 triangles and builds in 2.1 s.
- **Pictures:** `builder-styles-back`, `-front`, `-mantle` and the three `builder-woman-loose*` pictures were shot again.
### Needs eyes
- **The lift is modest.** Loose hair now has some body from the side and behind, and still lies close from the front. A centre parting would want the hair to rise from it. That needs the strands to leave the scalp at an angle, not only higher layers.
- **Stray beard cards on the chest.** With the mantle off, the man rolled from `b7` shows a scatter of beard cards lying on his tunic below the jaw. The fur collar hides them, but bare-necked dress shows them. This was so before these sessions. It is the next bodies fix in the builder.

## v80 — Session 878 — The beard stops at the tunic's collar (B3, a fix, prototype only)
Session 877 found this. A bearded man in a tunic, with no fur mantle, had a scatter of beard cards lying on his chest below the jaw. The beard's region of skin runs down the throat to rest height 0.60. The tunic covers the body up to 0.63, and its shader cuts it at 0.612. So about 3 cm of throat grew beard under the cloth. Those hairs are cards up to 7 cm long that fall with gravity, and their tips came out through the tunic onto the chest. The fur mantle's collar had hidden this in every earlier picture. It is still under FREEZE #297, so it touches only the prototypes.

The fix is in `makePerson`. When a tunic is worn, the beard's cards root only on triangles lying wholly above rest height 0.638 (`PACK.R.beardTunic`, made once). There are 1,602 of the 2,078 triangles. The same 520 cards are drawn from the same random stream, so the cloak drawn after the beard folds as it did. Without a tunic, the beard keeps the whole throat. The dark base shell under the beard is unchanged, since below the collar the tunic covers it.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 176 checks pass**, one of them new: **a beard over a tunic stops at its collar.**
  - The check builds the man rolled from `b7` with a beard of 0.8, in his tunic, with no mantle or cloak.
  - It reads the collar's front from the tunic's mesh at its cut, then counts beard points more than 4 cm below it and within 12 cm of the midline.
  - Session 877's code had 222 of 5,200 such points. This one has 0. The check was run on both to prove it tells them apart.
- **Pictures:** `builder-beard-tunic.jpg` and `builder-beard-tunic-before.jpg`, the same man from three-quarters front, and `builder-man-face.jpg` shot again.
### Needs eyes
- **The beard's lower edge** now ends on the collar's line. A long beard would hang over the collar and onto the chest, as a beard of its own grown from the jaw. The beard length is one slider (`beard`, 2 to 7 cm), so a long-bearded Markman would want that drape built.

## v80 — Session 886 — The temples thin out as the forehead does (B1, Michael's note on #272, prototype only)
Session 875 left one owed item. The hairline at the front of the head fades and thins, but the temples and the sides above the ears did not. There, the edge was simply where the hair's root region (`scalpRoots`) stops on a mesh edge. The dark under-shell ended in a hard stepped outline, and the strands started at full width on it. It showed as a step at the side of the brow on the man, and as a blocky dark edge above the woman's ear under a bun. This is still under FREEZE #297, so it touches only the prototypes (`people.js`, `builder.check.mjs`).

What changed in `people.js`:
- **A distance to the border, made once.** At load, the region's border is taken as the edges that only one of its triangles uses. Each vertex of the region gets its distance on the rest body to the nearest of those edges (`PACK.scalpEdge`), so every body reads the same numbers.
- **The shell fades and comes down at the sides.** The scalp shell reads that distance as an attribute.
  - From just behind the ear to the front of the temple, it fades from the skin's colour at the border to its own over 1.4 cm. The border wanders by ±3 mm of noise, as the forehead's does.
  - There it also comes down onto the skin, to 0.8 mm off it at the border from 2.5 mm, so its faded edge is no longer a ledge seen side-on by the ear. The first try lowered the shell all round. That drew the region's jagged front edge across the forehead as a shade, so the lowering is kept to the sides.
- **Strands at the sides are finer near the border.** Within 1.5 cm of the border, a strand's card narrows, down to 0.35 of its width at the edge, as at the front. The forehead keeps Session 875's measure. Nothing new is drawn from the random stream, so every style keeps its strands, and the cloak, drawn after the hair, folds as before.

## v80 — Session 899 — Card F9's seventh room: Aurenne's courtyard house round a fountain (prototype only)
The FREEZE (#297) holds. Michael answered all seven of this builder's open questions on 14 Oct, every one A. Six were "as drawn" (#316, #319, #320, #321, #322, #323), so there was nothing to build for them. #318's second part was "build the courtyard house next": OG-115's Aurenne panel leads with "a two-storey courtyard house round a fountain with arcades and blue tile", which the street's lots (6.4 to 9.6 by 6 to 8 m) cannot hold. So it is its own piece, a rich house for the better quarter, with its rooms built inside it as #303 set. OG-115 and OG-061 (the blue tile) were reread. The catalogue's notes on OG-115 flag only the Mark's "clans", which is not touched here.

**The house** (`aurenneCourtyard` in `pieces.js`, on Aurenne's kit):
- **The size:** 15 by 15 m, of two storeys (3.1 m to the upper floor).
- **To the street:** blank cream plaster under a stone cornice, a string course at the upper floor, and one arched door of 1.3 by 2.6 m in a frame of glazed tile. There are small barred windows below and four cedar lattice screens above, as the street houses have. The house looks in, not out.
- **The court:** its walls stand 3.6 m off the middle. Between them and a ring of columns 2.2 m off the middle runs a gallery on both floors:
  - below, three round arches a side on piers, each with a lathed stone column on its court face, and a tiled kerb round the open court;
  - above, cedar columns, a turned balustrade and the architrave the eaves rest on.
  - The open court is 4.4 m across. It holds a fountain (an octagonal basin faced in glazed tile, a stone rim, a pedestal with a bowl and a jet) and four orange trees in pots.
- **The roof:** one pantile roof in four slopes at 16°, from a parapet on the outer walls down to eaves over the upper gallery. The rain falls into the court. There are valleys of ridge tile at the corners, and cedar boards and rafters under it.
  - The tiles first came out wound to face down and read dark brown from above. They are wound to face up now, and the boards under them face down.
- **The plan:** four ranges round the court. The front range has the vestibule between two partitions. A masonry stair of 16 risers of 0.19 m climbs the west range's outer wall to a landing, and the upper floor is open over it where the head would meet it.
- **For the checks** the shell returns its walls' footprints cut at their doors, and its piers, columns, balustrade, stair rail, fountain and trees, each with its floor (`solids`). It also returns its doors and its roof's underside as a function (`under(x, z)`).
- The new materials (limestone paving, the upper floor's red tile, water, oranges) are added to the kit's Aurenne set, and no other piece reads them.

**The rooms** (`aurenneCourtyardHouse` in `rooms.js`):
- **Ground floor:**
  - the vestibule, tiled to 1.2 m, with a tiled masonry bench down each side and the street door's leaf hung open;
  - the store: seven oil jars down the street wall, sacks of grain and a chest;
  - OG-115's kitchen: a cooking bench of three braziers with a tiled top, a rail of seven copper pots hung over it, a bread oven in the corner, a work table with a board and a bowl, a water jar, and three shelves of blue and white plates;
  - the west range: the stair, a loom by the court wall with its weaver's bench, and two jars;
  - the dining room: a long table of 3 m with two benches, and a sideboard of plates and copper jugs;
  - across the back, the reception hall: divans on three walls with their cushions, two rugs, two brass tables with cups and a ewer, and a tile dado to 1.2 m broken at its doors.
- **Upstairs:**
  - the landing, with a chest and a rug;
  - the bedroom across the back: a bed of 2.18 m with its headboard, a chest either side, a table with a brass mirror, a comb and a jug, a stool, a divan, a rug and a tile dado;
  - the guest room;
  - the children's room: two small beds of 1.78 m, a toy chest, and a rocking horse on a rug;
  - a linen press of folded cloth;
  - the study: shelves of books, a lectern with an open book, and a divan under the lattices with a brass table and a lamp.
- **The lamps:** a lantern in every room, and four on brackets along each gallery.
- **The view:** `rooms.html?room=court`. `court` is the default, from inside the street door through the vestibule and the arcade to the fountain and the hall's arch. The others are `gallery`, `hall`, `kitchen`, `bedroom`, `study`, `children`, `outside` and `above`, with `&hour=`.

It follows the method Michael chose on #274 (*drapes hang, shells fit*), to his condition that no arm comes through. FREEZE #297 is still open, so this touches only the prototypes (`people.js`, `builder.check.mjs`, and the labels in `builder.js`).

What changed in `people.js`:
- **Mail is a garment colour, `mail`.** Worn over the tunic as a padded coat, it gives the person a padded tunic and a belt when they have none. It saves and loads, and shows on the page as "mail hauberk".
  - **Its body** is a shell off the tights, 9 mm over the tunic everywhere, and 2.1 cm over it below the belt, where it overlaps its own skirt. The sleeves are cut in the shader at rest |x| 0.3, which is the elbow (the elbow joint is at 0.313). Its neck is cut just under the tunic's, so the coat's collar shows.
  - **Its skirt** is a shell off the skirt helper, from under the belt to rest y −0.27, a hand above the knee (the knee is at −0.369). It stands 2.4 to 6.6 cm off the skirt shell, most at the hip, where the tunic's front stands out furthest. Over a long skirt it is 6 mm more.

Their edges are antialiased with `fwidth`. Where a pixel holds more than about a ring, the pattern gives way to its average grey, so it does not shimmer at a distance. The gaps are rougher than the rings.

On the mail's hem that threw a row of black teeth onto the thighs. The mail's two shells now cast through `cutDepth`, a depth material with the same cut. The older garments still cast their full regions; they were cut close enough that it did not show.

  - **The dome is fitted to the skull.** Round a centre at the rim's height, it takes the furthest point of the head in each of 72 × 24 directions, spreads it to its neighbours, smooths it four times without going below the spread, and adds 1.2 cm. The first try was an ellipsoid grown until it cleared the occiput. It came out 31 cm deep, a bowl on a stick.

  - **The hair is tucked short** under it, as under a hood. Unlike under a hood, the short cards are kept, and the dome is fitted round them with 4 mm to spare. Fitted round the head alone, a woman's tucked hair showed through the crown as gold flecks.
- **The tabard hangs over the mail.** `buildTabard` read the body, the tights and a skirt, but not the mail. In the first picture its front panel hung behind the mail skirt, and only a red lump showed through. Its outline now takes the mail's body and skirt by their own pushes, and its waist under the belt is 3.4 cm off the tights instead of 2.5.
- **`shellThrough`**, the robe's test of points against a garment's posed shell, is now a function of its own. The mail's test (`mailStats`) uses it too.

## v80 — Session 898 — A cloak hangs clear over mail (B2, prototype only)
Session 897 left one thing owed: a cloak over mail. 25 of 7,114 points of the mail's skirt came out through the back of a Markman's fur-collared cloak, up to 1.7 cm. From behind they showed as pale patches of mail through the cloth (`builder-armour-markman-back-before.jpg`, shot on Session 897's code at 1200 × 900). It is still under FREEZE #297, so this touches only the prototypes (`people.js`, `builder.check.mjs`).

Session 897 had tried raising the cloak's clearance where it lies on the body (`clearAt`), and the count did not move. So the points were not where the cloak lies on the back. They were where the folds are laid.
- A fold's trough comes in by at most the room between the column and the body's outline (`floorAt`). The hem then rises on the ridge and drops in the trough (`q.y += .45 * d * s⁴`).
- Over the mail skirt, which stands 4 to 7 cm out at the buttocks, the outline changes fast with height. A point that moved in at one height and then dropped a few millimetres ended up inside the outline at its new height.

The fix is one last pass at the end of `buildHang`. Every point of every column below the shoulders is held at least 4 mm outside the outline of what the cloak hangs over: the body, a skirt's shell, a robe's sleeves and now the mail, read from `wornMask` as before. Points already outside it do not move.
- Over mail it moves 548 of the cloak's points.
- Over the hooded habit (Session 888) it moves 71, each by under 4 mm.
- It moves none in the other cloak cases the check builds: the woman's cloak with the hood down, the short hooded cloak, and the fur-collared long cloak.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 221 checks pass.** The cloak over mail is a check again, where Session 897 only printed its count:
  - **0 of 7,114 points of the mail and the body are out through the cloak.**
  - **The habit under a hooded cloak** still passes: 0 of 6,413 points through, 3.7 cm clear.
  - The other cloaks are unchanged, measured outside the check: 0 points moved, and the same hem-in and fold depths.
- No page errors.
- **Pictures:**
  - `builder-armour-markman-back.jpg`: the Markman from behind, in a lighter cloak so the cloth reads. Nothing of the mail shows through.
  - `builder-armour-markman-back-before.jpg`: the same view on Session 897's code.
  - `builder-armour-markman.jpg` and `builder-robe-hooded.jpg` were shot again.
### Needs eyes
- **The back of a cloak over mail** now follows the mail skirt's outline at the buttocks wherever a fold would have cut into it. In the picture it reads as cloth over a stiff skirt. Whether the fold there looks pinched is for a closer look.
- This pass is a floor, not a drape. A cloak over plate, which stands further out and steps sharply, will want the folds laid against the outline at the height they end at, not the height they start at.

## v80 — Session 905 — F2a: the eleven suites CI found red (the deep-work session, card F2a)
The producer sent card F2a back: PR #315's CI on fde9867 failed eleven suites twice across seven shards (barberbox, coachinn, dragonsize, fiercewolf, hoardspot, homesleep, intreach, keepercone, shells, skirtlegs, wraithfloat). Main was merged in first (the backlog's one line kept both edits). Nine failed here too; barberbox and homesleep passed here and are left to the next CI run. Each was either a place where F2a broke behaviour, fixed in the code, or a suite that measured in the old unit, re-measured to the new truth. None was loosened.

**Fixed in the code.**
- **The wolves and the Cave Bear** (`fiercewolf`). Michael's A on #187 set them as shares of a man: a Wolf's back at 56% of one, a Dire Wolf's 73%, the bear's hump 88%. With the man 1.44 times taller, a Wolf's back fell back to 38% of him, the size #187 rejected. They are now drawn at their `play` size times `SCALE.BEAST` (07-scale.js, equal to `ROOM_K`, 1.444): Wolf 1.52, Snow Wolf 1.66, Dire Wolf 1.95, Ash Hound 1.44, Cave Bear 2.24. That puts them at 54%, 59%, 71%, 51% and 86% of a 1.76 m bandit. Only the drawing changes. A foe's `size`, and so its hits and reach, is unchanged (F2b). At the larger size a dead Dire Wolf came to rest standing in 1 of 120 seeded falls, and hit the four-second cap once. Stretching the ragdoll's clock by √k made it worse (3 standing, 6 capped), because its damping is per step. So a drawn-larger beast's fall now runs at its tuned size (its points and size divided by `rig.drawK`, the ground and walls read at K times, the bones aimed K times as far). That is S632's tuned fall exactly: 0 of 120 standing and 0 capped for both kinds. `beastfall`, `ragdoll` and `ragdollsearch` pass. The Faolchú (a Dire Wolf × 1.45 with arms of its own), the horses and the dragon keep their sizes; see below.
- **The health bars.** A person-bodied foe's bar stood at 1.3 × its scale, chest height on a 1.76 m man. It is now at 1.3 × `ROOM_K`. A beast of #187's bar is over its drawn back.
- **A wraith's glide** (`wraithfloat`). Its hover of .24 ± .05 was in the old unit, so the robe's hem came to 4.6 cm off the ground on the taller body. The hover is now × `ROOM_K`: 13.5 cm clear at the bottom of the bob.
- **The coaching inn's guests** (`coachinn`). `coachInnFolk` places them while the room is still in the kit's old unit, before `scaleRoom`. It tested with `intSolidAt`, whose step height (.62) is in metres. A table .47 high in the old unit was steppable there and stands .68 once scaled, so a traveller stood in it (Eilís, 2.6 cm inside a table's edge). The test now uses the heights the room will have.
- **A person under the crosshair beats a door that is only near** (`personAimedIn`, 50-travel.js; the prompt in 90-main.js reads the same rule). The door's exit zone is 1.6 deep and 3.2 wide, in metres, and in a room of true size it reaches the people waiting by the door. E at the coaching inn's driver, from one step behind them, walked you out of the inn. A bed already won the same way (S650).

**Re-measured** (the same claim, in the new unit):
- `dragonsize`: the dragon keeps its metres, under the lair's 4.4 roof (the dungeons' heights are F2b's). It now stands 2.09 bandits tall, which is "about twice a man's height", Michael's own words on #153. The old test asked for more than 2.7, three of the old 1.24 bandits.
- `fiercewolf`: the built scale is Michael's size × `SCALE.BEAST`; the shares of a man are unchanged.
- `skirtlegs`: r128's `boneTransform` gives a world point, so on a root now scaled 1.2 every distance read 1.2 times larger. The legs and the skirt are now read in the mesh's own frame, where its 2 cm bins and 5 cm limit were set. Worst pokes are 4.5, 4.2 and 4.5 cm (limit 5), at 4.2 to 6.8 vertices a frame (limit 9).
- `keepercone`: in a room of true size, 1.5 m east of the strongbox is across the counter, with no line of sight. The keeper now stands 1.5 m off on the first of sixteen bearings that has one.
- `hoardspot`: "looking at it, nearly level" (pitch −.25) from the 1.65 eye passed over the chest. It now aims at the chest's middle (−.73).

That rule runs in the kit's unit, before scaling, so it found two windows a side in a cabin 8 m deep where one is built, and a post at 5.3 m read as standing in front of a window. It now reads the windows as built, and checks it found them.

  - The faces are lime plaster, with brick showing in patches where it has fallen.

It is lined in red mortar, with a pale crust to 0.3 m where the water ran. It is dry and has no covers, so its bed is the walk: off the west terrace, in at the open mouth at x = −57, and east.

  - That pier is a stump 2.5 m tall on the string course, with loose blocks on its top.

## v80 — Session 908 — Card F8: Aurenne's trade tunnel (prototype only)
The FREEZE (#297) holds. This is the second of Aurenne's places from OG-121's panel, after the aqueduct (907): its "trade tunnels". I reread OG-121 and its row. The row flags the Aurennais ruins' "Roman" name and the crypts' dead, and neither touches a tunnel. The canon's Aurenne is a trading island of ports, so the tunnel is a road for goods through a headland, from a town's quay to the road inland. Whether it is that or a smugglers' run is asked (#335).

What is new in `places.js`:
- **`aurenneTunnel(o, r)`:** the quay's portal at z 0 faces +z, and the bore runs 56 m to the inland portal at z −56. It winds 1.6 m either side and runs straight for its last metres at either end, so each portal looks down it.
- **The bore:** one loft of its section along the line.
  - The floor is flat and 3.6 m wide, the walls upright to 2.4 m under a round vault (4.2 m at the crown).
  - The rock is pushed out from its line by up to 0.22 m by its own noise, never in, so the walk's width is a floor, not an average.
  - It is paved in 2 m lengths of limestone along the line, with two cart ruts 1.4 m apart and a gutter down the west side.
- **The lamps:** a plastered arched niche every 6 m on alternate walls, each with a dark back, a sill and a clay lamp. With `o.used` (default true) the lamps burn; with `o.used: false` they are out and you go by your torch.
- **The passing place:** midway the bore widens to 6 m for 6 m, with 3 m ramps either side, so two carts can pass.
  - Its walls are plastered to a dado under a band of blue glazed tile. The panels are turned to the bore's heading, because it curves most there.
  - It holds a stone bench, the tally-keeper's cedar table with a ledger and a stool, nine amphorae against the east wall, and two lamps on brackets.
  - A round shaft 1.2 m across rises through the rock to the sky. The vault is cut under it.
- **The portals:**
  - An arch in a plastered frame of 6.4 by 6.4 m, the opening a little wider than the bore's section.
  - An ashlar ring and jambs on its face, tiled spandrels and a blank tablet. What the tablet says is the quest writer's.
  - A cornice over it, let into a cliff face of 48 by 18 m.
  - The quay's paving lies before one portal and the dust road before the other.
- **Two corrections made during the session:**
  - The cliff's cut test added its 8 m lift once per vertex, three times over, so the cut never happened and the cliff stood across both arches. It now adds the lift once.
  - The first lamp spacing (7 m) left only five lamps, so it is now 6 m.
- **The view:** `places.html?place=tunnel` goes to `places-tunnel-view.js`. It has five views (`quay`, `tunnel`, `passing`, `inland`, `road`) and `&dark`. The lamps are small point lights, with the day down the shaft and a soft fill under it.

On the arm it builds as Session 904 left it (its six checks pass unchanged).

  - It leaves out the arms' skin and sleeves, so it passes between an arm and the side. It also leaves out the hair, the head and what the head carries, so it goes under long hair and stops at the neck. A cloak is kept, so over a cloak it goes over the cloak.

## v80 — Session 914 — Card F8: Aurenne's sea grotto (prototype only)
The FREEZE (#297) holds. Three answers came back first: Michael's A on #331 (the Mark's ice cavern is the cave's hall in ice), on #333 (the aqueduct stays broken) and on #335 (the trade tunnel is a road). All three say "as drawn", so nothing was built for them. Their entries move to Answered in `docs/decisions.md`.

This is the last of OG-121's Aurenne places that does not wait on the quest writer: its "sea grottoes". I reread OG-121 and its row, and OG-125's row for sea caves. Neither flag touches a grotto: the "Roman" name and the crypts' dead are not in it, and no diving gear is drawn. The grotto is built after the kind the islands' south has, a cave the sea made whose water glows. The day comes in through a drowned gate under the waterline and lights the water from below, while the arch above the water is low.

What is new in `places.js`:
- **`aurenneGrotto(o, r)`:** the sea at y 0, and the grotto along −z, built on the cave's own `caveHall`.
- **The stair:** a rock-cut way from a paved terrace under a cliff face, down 24 steps of 0.2 m on treads of 0.5 m. It is 2.6 m wide under a round vault, 3.7 m to the crown over the steps' noses, and level for its last 5 m.
  - At both ends it passes through an arched frame of plaster in a block let into the rock. The frame has an ashlar ring and jambs, tile panels, a tile band and a cornice.
  - The pick's noise pushes the rock out and never in, and it fades out where the frames stand.
- **The hall:** 60 m long, 37 to 40 m across 6 m up, and 18 to 27 m from the water to the roof near its middle. Below the high-water line the limestone is dark and wet.
- **The sea's ways in:** at the far end, a low arch 6.4 m wide and 3 m over the water, over a drowned gate 16 m wide and 7 m deep.
  - Beyond the gate lies a plane of daylit sea, so the gate shows blue through the water, not the sky.
  - The water is a blue that gives off its own light, broken into a net by a tiling texture of whole waves, over a pale sea floor.
- **The landing and the quay:**
  - The landing is paved across the near end at 1.2 m.
  - The quay runs 33 m down the east wall and is 3.6 m wide. Its sea face is ashlar down under the water, and the face's top is the coping.
  - Along the quay stand five bollards, with bronze rings on the face between them.
  - At its end, seven water stairs go down into the sea, with a skiff tied to them.
- **The spring:** at the landing's west end, against the rock.
  - A plastered block with a niche cut through it: a concave apse tiled in the blue zellige under a plastered half-dome, in an ashlar ring.
  - A bronze spout and a thread of water fall into an ashlar basin 2.4 by 1.3 m with its rim at 0.55 m. Benches stand either side.
  - What the spring is to anyone is the quest writer's.
- **The rest:** a beach of pale sand under the west wall across the water, 14 rocks breaking the surface, and short stalactites, none low over the walk.

Corrections made during the session:
- **The seabed was wound face down,** so it was invisible from above, and rays went through it. That accounted for 14 of the first run's leaks. It now faces up.
- **The skiff's shell was split along its length instead of being a bowl.** Its lathe was copied from the smugglers' lair's rowing boat, which I have not checked; it may be the same there. The skiff is now the lathe's lower half, laid along z.
- **The quay's paving slabs were turned about their centres** to follow the curving edge, which left wedge-shaped gaps where the edge bends fastest. They are now laid square behind the ashlar face's top, and the face follows the curve.
- **The apse's tiled half-cylinder bulged out of the wall.** It is now turned into the wall and seen from inside, in a plaster block with the niche cut through it, not a solid slab.
- **A dome lofted ring by ring closes to a point at its centre height, the hall's CY.** At 3 m that point lay inside the stair's opening, and the fan of large faces round it, kept because their centres fell outside the cut, covered the opening. The sight line up the stair failed on two of three keys.
  - CY is now 5.2 m, with the hall's lower radius 11 m, so the water is as deep.
  - The same fan at the far end held the arch's height anywhere between 2.2 and 5 m as the cut changed. The hall is now lofted in 208 rings, twice the cave's, which makes the fan about a metre across, so the arch's own cut decides its height.
- The paving and the floor under it fought at the same height; the floor now lies 8 cm under the paving.
- The terrace was blown out by a strong sun, now about half.
- **The view:** `places.html?place=grotto` goes to `places-grotto-view.js`. It has five views (`grotto`, `stair`, `quay`, `spring`, `back`). The light comes from blue lights under the water along the hall, a broad blue spot coming up through the gate, a thin white one at the arch, and the day down the stair.
### Verified (headless Chromium)

The shaft ran through 158 of the hand's 436 points. There were no checks. The spear is one of the two new kinds of weapon (Michael's 6 A on OG-028), and the guards of OG-025 and OG-044 carry one. FREEZE #297 is still open, so this touches only the prototypes (`people.js`, `builder.check.mjs`).

What changed in `people.js`:

  - It runs up the knuckles' line through the hole. That line is plumb, with a lean of 0 rad.

## v80 — Session 910 — The spear's fist closes round the shaft (L7, a fix to Session 909, prototype only)
**A correction to Session 909.** Its fist did not close round the shaft. Seen from the front, the four fingers stood straight up beside it, like a hand held up to stop someone. The checks passed anyway.

**Why.** The fingers were curled about their bones' own z axis, as every hand pose in `people.js` does. In this skeleton that axis is 36° off the knuckles' line, which is the real hinge.
- In the rest pose and in the shield's hanging fist, a turn about z still reads as a curl.
- In 909, the wrist was turned so the knuckles stand plumb. There, z lies 36° along the hand, so the "curl" lifted the fingers up the shaft.
- 909's hole search looked down the knuckles' line. Fingers stacked up that line fold into one ring in that view, so it found an enclosed hole that was not there.
- From the side (`builder-armour-spear-grip.jpg`), the fingers seemed to wrap the shaft.

What changed in `people.js`:
- **The fingers' hinge is the knuckles' line** (from the little finger's knuckle to the first finger's). It is read in the metacarpals' frame, and every finger bone hangs off its metacarpal unturned, so one axis serves all twelve.
- **The grip** (`fistGrip`, replacing `fistHole`):
  - The palm's facing is found by which way the middle fingertip moves as the hand closes.
  - With the fingers straight, the shaft (now always 2.6 cm) is laid in the palm's crease, 0.5 to 2.5 cm behind the knuckles. It sits as near the palm as the hand's points allow, 1 mm clear: 3.2 to 3.8 cm off the knuckles' bones.
  - The thumb's points (skinned more than half to its own bones) are left out of that. Placed with the thumb, the shaft stood 3.4 to 3.9 cm out, which pushed the fingers into it before they had closed.
- **The fingers close as a hand does:**
  - First all three joints of a finger bend together, in the shield's fist's proportions, 0.04 rad at a time, until a point of that finger would come inside the shaft.
  - Then the two outer joints go on alone, and then the last joint alone. Each stops a step short.
  - So each finger wraps round the shaft. Closing every finger as one block stopped at the first touch, with the fingertips against the front of the shaft (bends of 0.45 to 0.6). Closing the root joint fully first made a claw (1.26, 0.07, 1.13).
- **The thumb** is turned at its root through 33 trial turns (three axes, ±1 rad). It takes the turn that keeps it out of the shaft and brings it nearest round it.

The shield's fist (Session 906) curls about the same z axis, so its fingers are off their hinge too. With the arm hanging it reads closed in its pictures, so it is left as it is and noted below.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 238 checks pass.** The eight spear checks are sharper than 909's. Each now asks for:
  - no point of the hand inside the shaft, and none of the thumb's;
  - the nearest finger point within 2 mm of the shaft's surface;
  - each of the three joints bent more than 0.45 rad.
- For the eight spears:
  - The joints bend 0.70 to 0.78, 0.84 to 0.94 and 0.65 to 0.69 rad.
  - The fingers touch the shaft: the nearest point is 0.3 to 0.5 mm into its skin tolerance, inside the 1 mm allowed.
  - The thumb is 0.7 mm in to 1.2 mm off.
  - Nothing else of the person is within 15.6 to 30.0 mm of the shaft.
  - The wrist turns 0.33 to 0.38 rad.
- `kit.check.mjs` passes. No page errors.
- **Pictures:** the six `builder-armour-spear*.jpg` were shot again with the closed fist.
### Needs eyes
- **The shield's left fist** (Session 906) curls about the bones' z, not the knuckles' line. It wants the same hinge. Its pictures read closed, so it was not touched.
- **The thumb** lies along the shaft or against it. It does not cross over the first finger as a hard grip's does.

## v80 — Session 921 — Card F8: the Gatelands' monastic ruin (prototype only)
OG-121's Gatelands panel lists "round cairns, monastic ruins and limestone caves". The cairn (Sessions 869 and 884) and the cave (872 and 882) are built. This is the monastic ruin, built after the island's own: a ring of dry stone round a green, a roofless church, a round tower, a ringed high cross and the brothers' beehive cells. I reread OG-121 and its row. Its flags concern the crypts' dead and Aurenne's "Roman" ruins, and neither touches this. The canon calls monasteries lore-neutral atmosphere (`lore_canon.md`, the fort catalogue), and the backlog's Gatelands target already names high crosses. No graves are built, since §3.1 gives the dead to the gates. Who the brothers were and why they left is the quest writer's. FREEZE #297 is still open, so this touches only the prototypes (`places.js`, `places-abbey-view.js`, `places-view.js`, `places.check.mjs`).

What is new in `places.js`, `gatelandsAbbey(o, r)`. The green is level at y 0, the gate is on +z and the altar to the east (+x):
- **The ground:** level inside the ring and for 3 m outside it, then falling away at 7 in 100, lumpy.
- **The cashel:** a dry-stone ring 61.6 m across and 1.4 m thick, battered on both faces, its head 1.9 to 2.2 m up.
  - It has fallen to 0.6 m in two breaches, and its stones lie spilled either side.
  - A new helper, `ringWall`, builds any ring of dry stone from an angle to an angle with its head at h(a). The fallen cell uses it too.
- **The gatehouse:** two round arches 2.6 m wide and 3.6 m high, 7 m apart, between side walls 4 m high. It is roofless and paved, with dressed stone at the arches.
- **The church:**
  - A nave of 12 by 6.4 m inside, with walls 0.9 m thick and 5 m high under gables of 9.4 m.
  - A round-headed west door, 1.4 by 2.6 m.
  - A chancel arch, 3 by 4.2 m, into a chancel of 5.5 by 4.4 m, with an east window over a block of stone for an altar.
  - Splayed round-headed windows: two in the nave's south wall, one in its north wall, one in the chancel's south wall, and one high in the west gable.
  - The walls are built by a new `wall(L, T, top, holes)`: a face drawn in its own plane with a ragged head and arched holes, then stood up. `dressArch` sets the dressed ring and jambs round the doors and arches.
  - Roofless. The wall-heads are ragged, and the nave's south wall has fallen to about 1.3 m over 3.5 m, its stones in the grass outside.
- **The round tower:**
  - 26 m of shaft, 5.2 m across at its foot and 4.4 at its head, on a plinth, under a stone cone to 30.4 m.
  - Its door is 3.2 m up, turned to face the church's west door, in a frame of jambs, lintel and sill. Three slits climb the shaft, and four windows sit under the cap.
- **The high cross:** 4.5 m on a two-stepped base, its arms in a ring 1.32 m across, with raised panels on the shaft.
- **The cells:**
  - Three corbelled huts, 6 m across and 4 m high, built as two lathe shells, the inner one 4 m across and 3.3 m high. The door is cut through both shells and closed with jambs and a lintel stone.
  - Two are whole, their doors (0.9 by 1.9 m) turned to the green. One has fallen to its lower courses, with its stones heaped inside.
- **The rest:** the footings of a long range of 14 by 7 m, where the brothers ate, with a gap for its door; a yew in the green; ash trees outside the ring.
- 73,420 triangles in 12 draws.

The view: `places.html?place=abbey` goes to `places-abbey-view.js`. Its views are `abbey`, `gate`, `nave`, `tower`, `cross` and `cells`, under a low autumn sun in the south-west with a thin mist.

## v80 — Session 915 — F2a: CI's third round, one suite and the hour (the deep-work session, card F2a)
Session 905 left PR #315 with main merged in (3748198) and CI's run 38675675725 still going. That run passed ten of twelve shards on all 377 suites they ran but one: `homesleep`, which failed twice in shard 2, as it had in the first round on fde9867, where it passed here and was left to CI. Shards 5 and 12 failed nothing. Each was cut at the job's hour on its last suite (`waylamp`, `wolfcloak`), with every suite before it green. Main was merged in again (7 commits, docs and prototypes only, nothing under `js/`, `index.html` or `tests/`).

**`homesleep`, re-measured.** At 22h and at 6h the resident is awake, and the suite asks that they "see across the room as before". It sweeps the room's free spots more than 2.3 m from the bed and asks that at least one is seen. Indoors a person sees in a 120° cone about the way they face (S368), and the resident ambles. In the cottage 1.8 times too wide there were always spots in front of them. In a cottage of true size there are eleven, and a resident who has ambled to face a wall has none of them in front: CI read 0 of 11 at both hours, and this machine read 2 and 5. Nothing in the game is wrong; the snapshot was. The sweep now turns the awake resident to face the middle of the room first, and the claim is stronger than before: at least a third of the spots seen (7 of 11 at both hours here), not more than none. The asleep sweep is unchanged (they see nothing, whichever way they lie).

**The hour.** The suites add up to 598 minutes on CI, about 50 a shard of twelve, against the job's 60. The sharder's table was refreshed in Session 745, and 34 suites since then were not in it at all and were counted as 60 s. Some had grown: renewal took 339 s where 219 was counted, hourhitch 391 for 286, reader 329 for 272, autosave 185 for 129, pauseleaf 248 for 157. So shard 12 planned 52 minutes and ran 59½. One suite's time also moves by a third between runs on the same code (scaleratio: 567 s on d9616ac's run, 357 s on this one). `tests/run.mjs`'s table is now this run's 377 times plus shard 12's from its suite headers; the 39 suites the run did not time (shard 5's, cut short) keep their old numbers. CI runs fourteen shards, not twelve (`.github/workflows/check.yml`, the matrix and `--shard=k/14`), which comes to 43 minutes a shard, as Session 652 went from eight to twelve. Not loosened: no suite is skipped and the job's limit stays 60.

A correction: Session 905 has two entries, this card's and the bodies builder's shield (B2, prototype). Both were written the same night on different branches; the numbers are left as they are, and this entry is 915, one above the highest on main and the builders' branches.

## v80 — Session 917 — The cloak's outside was in its own shadow (B2, a fix, prototype only)
Session 916's pictures showed every cloak nearly black from the front: the Gatelander's green, the Aurennais' tan and the Markman's brown. The tunic, the apron and the skirt under them were lit by the same key light. Every committed cloak and cape picture since the cloak was built (Sessions 836 to 841) shows the same. Turning off the cloak's `receiveShadow` lit it, so the cloak was shadowing itself.

The cause is the winding of the cloak's sheet. Its columns go round the neck and its rows go down. With the triangles wound `a, a+1, b`, `computeVertexNormals` gave normals pointing into the body: 0 to 1.7% of the points of five test cloaks pointed out. The material is double-sided, so the shading flips them on the face that is seen and the shading itself was right. But three.js moves a point's shadow lookup along the vertex normal before it reads the shadow map (`normalBias`, 0.02 in the builder). On the cloak's outside, that put the lookup 2 cm behind the cloak, inside its own shadow.

What changed in `people.js`:
- The cloak's sheet and its embroidered hem band are wound the other way (`a, b, a+1`), so their normals point out.
- Nothing else reads these normals: the hang, the clearances and the strap all work on the columns' points.
- The tabard's front panel was already wound outward, which is why it read lit. Its back panel faces away from the key light, so it is left as it is.

**Correction to Session 916:** its note that the Aurennais man's full cloak "hangs as a box" was half this. Lit, the folds show and it reads as cloth. It still stands stiffly off his chest; that is the hang's own shape on a broad build, and stays owed.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`builder.check.mjs`: all 257 checks pass.** There are five new ones, one for each test cloak (a hood down, a hood up, a fur collar, a cape with an embroidered hem, a plain cape). Each checks that its normals point out of it, read round the vertical axis through its own middle:
  - **Now:** 98.3 to 100% of the points, and 100% of the hem band's.
  - **The same check on the old `people.js`:** all five fail, at 0 to 1.7%.
  - The cloaks' other checks (the clearance from the body, nothing through it, the hang) pass with the same numbers.
- `kit.check.mjs` passes. No page errors.
- **Pictures:** the 25 that show a cloak or a cape were shot again: `builder-cloak-*`, `builder-cape-*`, the slung shields, `builder-armour-markman*`, `builder-armour-spear-cloak` and `builder-robe-hooded`. The others are left as committed. Rendering is not byte-identical between runs, so a full re-shoot changes every file, and the hair pictures also pick up a horizon change from an earlier session.
### Needs eyes
- **The cloaks are seen for the first time as their colours.** The folds laid in Sessions 839 and 840 now show from the front, and some read as stiff and vertical where they were hidden in black before. That is the hang's work to answer, not this fix's.
- **In the game,** the townsfolk's cloaks are built by `32-people.js`, not this kit, so this changes nothing there. When F4 carries the kit's cloak in, it carries the outward winding with it.

## v80 — Session 932 — The giant spider's thorns and egg sacs (L4, prototype only)
The last of OG-041's classic five that already stood in the kit: the giant spider (Session 772) had the sheet's pale bulbous abdomen, dark legs and cluster of red eyes, but not its thorny legs or its egg sacs. The sheet draws both, so this asks nothing new. FREEZE #297 is still open, so this touches only the prototypes (`creatures.js`, `creatures.check.mjs`, `bestiary.js`).

What changed in `creatures.js`:
- **A leg may be thorny.** `thorns: { per, len, r, rake }` on a leg pair sets short dark spines up every segment past the hip, on the segment's upper and outer faces, each raked toward the foot and shorter toward the tip, placed by the seed. A segment's thorns are one merged mesh, rigid on its bone, so eight legs add 24 meshes, not 88.
- **`eggs`, a new part: a clutch of egg sacs under a tail.** A spider's abdomen is the kit's tail, so the sacs sit along its underside toward the tip (`at`, the stretch of the tail; `drop`, how far down its girth; `spread`, how far round the sides). Each sac is a lumpy silk ball (noise on a sphere, a faint wrapped banding), merged per tail bone. `P.tail` now records its points and radii for parts after it.
- **The spider wears both:** about 3.7 thorns a segment, 88 in all, 4 to 10 cm long; seven sacs of 9 to 15 cm in a tight clutch at the abdomen's tip, white silk against the pale hide. The bits are 880 triangles of thorns and 1,764 of sacs beside the hide's 84,528.
- `bestiary.js` takes `?cam=back`, a low rear three-quarter view, to show the clutch.

The `drop` is larger than the capsules suggest (1.4 of the tail's radius): the grown flesh blends its capsules outward, so at 1.0 the sacs sat inside the skin and showed only as white patches. A part placed before the flesh is grown cannot read the surface; if more parts need to sit on the skin, a pass after growth that pushes bits out to it would be the fix.

### Verified (headless Chromium)

  - Seven egg sacs, clear of the ground (lowest 0.20 m) and below the abdomen's tip in all 72 poses of the walk, the trot and the stand.

## v80 — Session 934 — The skeleton: a bare body (L4, prototype only)
The last of OG-041's classic five: a skeleton with a notched sword and a round wooden shield. Canon §9a puts skeletons in Solas and Uisce gates. The kit grows one smooth skin over its capsules, and a skeleton has none, so this session gives the kit a second kind of hide. The sheet draws the skeleton, so this asks nothing new. FREEZE #297 is still open, so this touches only the prototypes (`creatures.js`, `creatures.check.mjs`).

What changed in `creatures.js`:
- **A plan may be `bare`.** Instead of growing the flesh, `bareGeo` draws each capsule as the bone it stands for.
  - A limb's capsule becomes a shaft with a knob at each end.
  - The spine's, neck's and tail's capsules become a stack of vertebrae.
  - The head's and jaw's capsules stay whole, as the skull.
  - The pieces are skinned by the same `dressFlesh` as any hide, so each moves with its bone and every skin weight still sums to one.
  - One catch: `capDist` reads a capsule's `sm`, which `growFlesh` sets. Without it every colour came out NaN, so the first picture was black. `bareGeo` now sets it too.
- **`ribs`, a new part:** a cage of arcs off the spine (`n` a side), each running round the side and forward, stopping short of a breastbone. They are widest mid-cage and drop as they go. With `pelvis`, two flared hip blades sit on the first spine bone.
- **`gear` takes a sword:** a flat blade narrowing to its point, its edges notched at rows the seed picks, with a crossguard, a leather grip in the fist and a pommel. A shield now takes its own `tone` and `rim`.
- **`skeleton`, the Skeleton:** an upright biped with a man's proportions, its skull 1.66 m up.
  - It has 14 ribs, dark eye sockets and a hinged jaw.
  - It carries a 0.7 m notched sword in its right hand, point down and ahead, and a 0.3 m wooden shield rimmed in iron on its left forearm.
  - 23 bones and 6,324 triangles, half the troll's hide.
  - It walks with the troll's biped gait.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`creatures.check.mjs`: all 991 checks pass** (981 before).
  - The skeleton's gaits pass: every foot reaches its target, the walk's feet are down 0.69 of 0.68 and the trot's 0.46 of 0.45.
  - It is bare, with 14 ribs.
  - Its sword and shield stay clear of the ground in all 72 poses (lowest 0.107 m). The first try, with the point 55° down, put it 2.6 cm into the floor; 40° fixed it.

  - `creatures-skeleton.jpg` (side) and `creatures-skeleton-front.jpg`.

## v80 — Session 941 — The crossbow (L7, prototype only)
L7's new kinds of weapon are the spear and the crossbow first (Michael's 6 A). The spear has been in the kit since Session 909; this is the crossbow. Each island has its own make by L7's rule (the Gatelands wood, bone and leather; the Mark stone and iron; Aurenne fine metal and carving), so this asks nothing new. FREEZE #297 is no longer open, but the bodies stay out of the game until F4, so this touches only the prototypes (`people.js`, `builder.js`, `builder.check.mjs`).

What changed in `people.js`:
- **`buildCrossbow`: carried point down in the right fist.** The fist is the spear's (Sessions 909 to 912): the forearm forward, the knuckles plumb, the fingers closed round a round grip 26 mm thick. The tiller runs plumb through it. The butt rises to about the chest (1.38 to 1.59 m) and the prod and stirrup hang by the shin (34 to 55 cm off the ground). The prod spans fore and aft, turned 16° about the tiller so its back tip swings out from the thigh, and the bolt's face looks out from the body. It is unspanned: the string is braced across the tiller's top and there is no bolt.
- **The tiller is one swept tube** (`sweepTube`, `tillerAt`). It is round in the fist, squared ahead of it to the prod, and deepens and drops toward the belly behind it into a stock 10 cm deep. The same section function builds the mesh and tests what is inside it.
- **Its fittings:** a nut half sunk in the top, the bolt's groove, a long trigger lever under the belly ahead of the fingers, a bridle binding the prod on fore and aft, and an iron stirrup at the front.
- **`CROSSBOWS`, the make by island**, chosen by the people or by `crossbowMake`:
  - **The Gatelands:** a 66 cm yew prod lashed on with three turns of cord a side, a bone nut. 5,536 triangles.
  - **The Mark:** a 60 cm iron prod, flatter, in an iron bridle, an iron nut. 5,056 triangles.
  - **Aurenne:** a 64 cm lacquered prod of horn and sinew with pale horn tips, bound in gold, with gold ferrules at the grip and the heel, a bronze nut and stirrup. 5,856 triangles.
- A full cloak is thrown back off the right shoulder for the crossbow as for the spear. A spear and a crossbow asked together give the spear.
- `crossbow` (the tiller's wood) is a garment colour and `crossbowMake` a dress flag, so a genome saves and loads it; the page lists it as *crossbow tiller*.
- A first try had the butt starting 8 cm above the grip's middle, where the thumb sits: 14 points of a hand inside it. The grip now runs to 11.5 cm. A first prod of 70 cm for Aurenne put its back tip 3.6 mm into a man's thigh; it is 64 cm now, and turned.

## v80 — Session 943 — Rags at the skeleton's hips: the first cloth on a creature (L4, prototype only)

What changed in `creatures.js`:

  - The strips flare 3.5 cm out as they fall, and darken toward the foot.
- **How a strip moves:** its top is on the hip bone. Any strip off the middle hangs over a thigh, so it passes to that thigh's bone down its length (a smoothstep, up to 0.7 of the weight at the foot). It swings with the leg, and the leg does not walk through it.
  - A first try put the lower half wholly on the thigh. The edge between the halves stretched to 2.2 times its length at the trot; a smooth blend at full weight still made 1.57. At 0.7 the worst is 1.27.
- **`sheetGeo` takes a second bone:** a sheet's point may carry `blend: [bone, weight]`. The fins, weed and leaves are unchanged, each point on one bone.
- **On the skeleton:** 11 places for strips, 30 cm long and 7.5 cm wide, in dirty linen, on a leather cord. The seed leaves 10 of them.
  - The plan's sheets are opaque now (`finOpacity: 1`); the drowned skeleton keeps its 0.95.
  - The drowned skeleton wears them too, in weed-dark cloth, 8 strips by its seed.

## v80 — Session 944 — The goblin's scrap-leather harness: straps on grown skin (L4, prototype only)
OG-041 draws its goblin in a scrap-leather harness. Session 933 owed it because nothing could lie on a creature's grown skin: the flesh is grown after the parts are laid, so a part cannot know where the surface will be. Session 943's rags hang free from a cord and did not need to know. Only the prototypes are touched (`creatures.js`, `creatures.check.mjs`).

What changed in `creatures.js`:
- **A part may lay something on the finished skin.** It pushes a function onto `B.after`, which `build` runs once the flesh is grown and its weights are read.
- **`straps`, a new part: a harness laid on the skin.**
  - Each strap is a path of (t, angle) pairs round the spine: t runs from the hip at 0 to the chest at 1, and angle 0 is the belly. It is drawn as a ribbon of a given width.
  - Each point of the path finds the furthest skin point within 2.5 cm along the spine and 9° round it, and stands 7 mm outside it.
  - Each point also takes that skin point's four bone weights, so the strap moves exactly as the skin under it does.
  - `sheetGeo` takes a sheet's own per-point weights (`skin`) for this.
  - (The name `harness` was the draught horse's collar of Session 867; a second `P.harness` silently replaced it on the first try, and the goblin built none.)
- **On the goblin:**
  - A belt round the hips, 10 cm wide (the goblin is built at the troll's size and halved, so 5 cm as it stands).
  - A sash from the right shoulder across the chest to the left hip and round the back.
  - A patch of pale hide on the right shoulder.
  - 119 points in three straps.
  - Its sheets are opaque.

### Verified (headless Chromium)
- **`creatures.check.mjs`: all 1,008 checks pass** (1,007 before).
  - The goblin's three straps are laid on the skin at 119 points, none missed.
  - Through every pose of the walk, the trot and the stand, each strap point's distance to the skin point under it stays within 0.83 to 1.16 of its distance at rest.
- The goblin's gaits and gear pass as before.
- Pictures: `creatures-goblin.jpg` re-shot; `creatures-goblin-front.jpg` re-shot; `creatures-goblin-back.jpg` (new).

### Needs eyes
- **At this range** the harness reads as a belt and a sash. The hide patch on the shoulder is small, and mostly hidden behind the shield arm from the front.
- **The straps are flat ribbons:** no buckles, no stitching, no thickness at their edges.
- **What's next:** the method could also strap the troll's lashed-on armour scraps (OG-041) and a beast's saddle girth.

## v80 — Session 946 — Card F9's fifteenth room: the Gatelands temple (prototype only)
The shrine is next on L5's list after the guildhall (939), which waits on #352. OG-043 draws the Gatelands temple as a small stone church with a statue inside. The canon (§4.1) says what it is for: the Irish-register culture worships the six makers by their work, and "six have temples … each with a statue and a boon in its domain". So this is a temple of one of the six gods. It is drawn for An Teallach, the Hearth, the god of towns, by default; `o.god` gives any of the six their icon (the hull, the sundial, the wolf, the gate, the lamp, the shuttle, from the canon's table). The Church of the Weaver is Aurenne's (the Compact), and the Guest has no shrine, so neither is drawn here. FREEZE #297 is closed and F2a has merged, but this is still a prototype under the run's order (rooms first, then into the game). It touches only `pieces.js`, `rooms.js`, `rooms-view.js` and `rooms.check.mjs`.

**The house** (`GL_PLANS.temple` in `pieces.js`) is the kit's first building with its door in a gable:
- One high storey, 9.6 by 6 m, of bare rubble 0.75 m thick, 3.8 m to the wall plate, under slate at 50°. There is no chimney and no gutter.
- A round-headed door 1.15 by 2.65 m stands in the west gable, under voussoirs. Each long wall has two round-headed slits, and the east gable has a round-headed window at 2.95 m, over the statue.
- The gables first had the forge's parapets. At 0.75 m of wall their kneelers grew into battlements, so the temple's gables are plain under the slate's verge.
- The plank door now takes `ajar` as the transom door does (Session 893), so the room can hang its own leaf, open.

**The room** (`gatelandsTemple` in `rooms.js`):
- **The dais** is one step of 0.18 m across the east end.
- **The statue** stands on a plinth of 0.5 m on the dais, 2.05 m of carved limestone. It is a robe turned on a lathe, a hooded head, and arms bent to hold the god's icon before its breast, facing the door. Its head is under the east window's sill, so the window lights it from behind and above. The Hearth's lamp holds a real flame, with its own small light on the page.
- **Offerings** lie at the statue's feet: bread, a bowl of grain, shells and marigolds.

## v80 — Session 949 — The Gatelands' tower mill (card F8, prototype only)
L5's "roads and works" (OG-046: farms and windmills, shipyards, lighthouses, canals, toll gates, mines, aqueducts, ferries, watchtowers) has had only the mine (857) and the aqueduct (907). The windmill is the first of the rest. It is the Gatelands' tower mill of the south-east coast's kind: a whitewashed round tower with a thatched cap, which OG-014's whitewashed country asks for. It is a work in the land, not a house, so it lives in `places.js` beside the aqueduct and the abbey, with its own view (`places-mill-view.js`, dispatched from `places-view.js`). Nothing new is asked. It touches only `places.js`, the two views and `places.check.mjs`.

**The mill** (`gatelandsMill` in `places.js`, at true size, its front door to +z):
- **The tower:** rubble, limewashed, battered from 6 m across at the foot to 4.6 m at the curb 9 m up, on a tarred plinth.
  - Two round-headed doors, 1.05 by 2.15 m, under dressed heads, front and back, each with a step. The miller can come and go whichever way the sails face.
  - Eight small windows turn up the tower over four floors. Each opening is laid on the wall's batter and stands just proud of it.
- **The cap:** an ogee of thatch on a timber curb, with a finial. The old Irish mills were thatched so.
- **The windshaft** comes out of the cap's front at 6° up. The hub is 4.2 m from the tower's axis.
- **Four commons sails:** a stock 8.6 m from the hub, and a lattice 1.9 m wide on the trailing side from 1.6 m out.
  - On a working day the cloth is spread over the lattice. With `&rest` (`o.working` false) it is furled along the stock and the bare lattice shows.
- **The tail pole** runs from the cap's back down to a cart wheel 9.5 m behind the cap, braced either side. By it the miller turns the cap into the wind.
- **At the door:** a worn-out millstone leaned on the wall, and three sacks of meal. A path of stone leads to the lane over a knoll that falls gently away.
- 11,108 triangles in 14 draws; 19.2 m from the ground to a sail's tip.

`o.wind` turns the cap and `o.angle` turns the sails. The builder also returns `sailPts(θ)`, the sails' outline at any turn, for the checks.

The view: `places.html?place=mill`, with `view=mill` (from the lane), `sails` (under them by the door), `back` (the tail pole and its wheel) and `far`, plus `&rest`.

## v80 — Session 967 — The Gatelands' lighthouse (card F8, prototype only)
L5's "roads and works" (OG-046: "lighthouses and beacons"; OG-058's waystations list one too) has had the mine (857), the aqueduct (907) and the windmill (949). The lighthouse is next. The Gatelands' register is Irish, so the precedent is Hook Head, the old lighthouse on its promontory in Wexford: a squat round tower, limewashed, with two black bands, a gallery on corbels and a lantern on its head, and the keepers' houses in a walled yard. It is a work in the land, so it lives in `places.js` beside the mill, with its own view (`places-lighthouse-view.js`, dispatched from `places-view.js`). Nothing new is asked. It touches only `places.js`, the two views and `places.check.mjs`. The one import added to `places.js` is the kit's `gatelandsBuilding` and `GL_PLANS` from `pieces.js`.

**The lighthouse** (`gatelandsLighthouse` in `places.js`, at true size, the sea to +z):
- **The headland:** a promontory of turf over a ragged cliff that falls 14 m to the sea. The break is 12.5 m out on the mean, its line roughened by bearing, and runs on inland as a neck. Rocks lie along the break. The ground is two grids, a metre round the headland and three metres inland. The coarse one is tucked under the fine one so no crack shows at the seam.
- **The tower:** limewashed rubble, battered from 7.6 m across at the foot to 6.6 m at the gallery 20 m up, on a tarred plinth, with two tarred bands.
  - A round-headed red door of 1.1 by 2.3 m faces landward on a step.
  - Six small windows climb the stair's turn.
- **The gallery:** a stone deck 1 m wider than the tower on 24 corbels, and an iron railing of 1.05 m on 32 standards.
- **The lantern:**
  - a stone pedestal, and a glazed room of twelve sides, 1.4 m round and 2.4 m high, its astragals painted red;
  - inside, the lamp on its column within a glass lens;
  - a copper dome gone green, a ventilator ball, and a vane.
  - With `o.lit`, the lamp burns. At night the page adds its light and a faint beam out to sea.
- **The keeper's house:** the kit's thatched cottage (`GL_PLANS.cottage`), landward, its front to the tower. It stands in a yard behind a low rubble wall, and a flagged path runs from the tower's door to its door.
- 26,516 triangles in 15 draws, and the cottage's 11. The lamp is 36.3 m over the sea and 26.2 m from the headland to the vane.

The view: `places.html?place=lighthouse`, with `view=light` (from the landward neck), `sea` (from the water under the cliff), `gallery` (by the lantern) and `far` (from along the coast), plus `&night`.

## v80 — Session 946 — bellwreck waits for its port's discovery (QA)
The QA routine's first item with FREEZE #297 closed and F2a merged: the FLAKY suites whose test fixes were owed. `bellwreck` cost the most, two retries on 15 Oct (main's 69e0c91 and F2a's ce23dbe), each on the check *within forty units at high tide, A mast stands up out of the sea…, once*, whose list of things said held the mast's line and *Carrigcarra discovered · +50 XP*. The suite stands the player at the bell's port until the wreck is built, and stopped waiting the moment `BELL_WRECK` existed. The port itself is discovered by `tickDiscovery` (`js/83-world-generator.js`), which runs every half second over `SITES`, the loaded cells' sites only: on a slow runner the wreck could be built before the port's cell had loaded or the half second come round, and the toast then fired while the player stood by the mast, inside the window the check counts. The game is right (you are near the port); the test was waiting for the wrong thing. The wait now runs until the wreck is built and `discovered(P.port)` is true, and a check says the port was found before the wreck was visited. The mast check keeps its *once* and its single line: nothing was loosened.
### Verified (headless Chromium)

## v80 — Session 947 — carraignight waits for the door, not the clock (QA)
`carraignight` went FLAKY once on 15 Oct (run 38695728480, shard 11): the street half passed, then the indoor loop threw at its first `page.evaluate` with `WORLD.settle.get('carraig_mor')` undefined, several homes in. The loop went into eight homes at eight hours each, paced by fixed waits: 1.5 s after `goToInterior`, 0.8 s after `exitInterior`. Both moves happen only in `doFade`'s callback, a 440 ms `setTimeout` (`js/20-quests.js`), which a loaded runner can fire late. When it did, the next step found the last room's `INT_BOX` still set with `lid` still the overworld, put the player at room coordinates (0 to the room's width) in the open world, and the next `WORLD.tick` dropped Carraig Mór as thousands of units away. The game was right to; the test had moved the player there. The loop now waits for `isInterior()` and `currentHouse` being this home after going in, and for `lid==='overworld'` after coming out, and throws rather than moving the player to `INT_BOX` when not indoors. The checks and their hours are unchanged.

## v80 — Session 948 — coopsaves waits for the game's own saves to land (QA)
`coopsaves` went FLAKY once (run 38653460071, 14 Oct): *the old save loads to the same state* loaded the first character (gold 777, level 7) instead of the hand-written v2 save (gold 4242, level 9). Step 2 Continues the first character and lets it run 12 s; step 3 writes the old one-row save, calls `ssSetActive('oldone_manual_2')` and reloads. `ssWrite` (`js/70-saves.js`) sets the active key in its `.then`, when the write lands, so a save from step 2 still in flight landed after step 3's call and pointed Continue back at the first character. The test waited for nothing between the two. It now wraps `ssWrite` before clicking Continue to count the writes in flight, holds the autosave off (`SS.lastAuto`) once the character is hidden, and waits for the count to reach 0 before step 3. No check changed. The game's half, that a late autosave can re-point Continue after you load another save from the menu, was already filed in backlog I for the systems builder.
Correction to Session 947: its *Verified* left the new look's run to the PR comment; `carraignight --look=new` passed, every check.

## v80 — Session 971 — Aurenne's coastal watchtower (card F8, prototype only)
L5's "roads and works" (OG-046: "watchtowers and forts") has had the mine (857), the aqueduct (907), the windmill (949) and the lighthouse (967). OG-124's Aurenne panel draws "a coastal watchtower", and the canon gives it a reason: piracy is the Mark's undeclared war, and the Compact's tithe-ships are its favourite prey. So the Compact keeps a chain of towers along its coast, each in sight of the next. The precedent is the Genoese and Saracen towers of the Tyrrhenian coast and the borj of the Maghreb, which fits Aurenne's Mediterranean and North African register: a round tower on a scarp, its door high up, a stair that stops short of the door, a parapet on corbels, a beacon on the roof. It is dressed in Aurenne's own materials (§1.3, and the catalogue's note on OG-124 against Tuscan stone): cream lime plaster, limestone dressings and a band of blue tile. It lives in `places.js` beside the lighthouse, with its own view (`places-watchtower-view.js`, dispatched from `places-view.js`). Nothing new is asked. It touches only `places.js`, the two views and `places.check.mjs`.

**The tower** (`aurenneWatchtower` in `places.js`, at true size, the sea to +z):
- **The point:** dry turf over a rock edge that falls 11 m to the sea, the break 13 m out on the mean and ragged by bearing. Rocks lie along it, and two cypresses stand inland.
- **The scarp and the drum:** a scarp battered from 10 m across at the foot to 8.4 m at a limestone cordon 4 m up. Above it a near-upright drum rises to the terrace at 12.3 m, with six slit windows.
- **The parapet:** under it, a band of blue tile. Twenty limestone corbels of three courses carry it 0.65 m out, the gaps between them dark: the machicolations, for dropping stones on whoever is at the door. It stands 1.05 m over the terrace, with ten loopholes.
- **The door and the stair:**
  - the door is round-headed, 1.0 by 2.1 m, in limestone jambs and a ring, its sill 5.4 m up on the landward side;
  - a solid masonry stair of 27 risers of 0.2 m on 0.3 m treads climbs beside the tower to a landing pier 1.1 m short of the wall;
  - a gangway of four planks crosses the gap. With `o.drawn` it is taken in, the gap stands open and the blue leaf is shut;
  - while the gangway is down, the door stands open.
- **The terrace:** paved in limestone. The stair's head is in a small hut of 1.5 m under a little dome. The beacon is an iron basket on three legs on a stone plinth, loaded with faggots; `o.lit` lights it.
- **Inland:** a flagged path from the stair's foot, and the cistern's wellhead.
- 20,408 triangles in 13 draws.

The view: `places.html?place=watchtower`, with `view=tower` (from the path inland), `door` (on the landing), `roof` (on the terrace by the beacon), `sea` (from the water under the point) and `far` (from along the coast), plus `&drawn` and `&night`.
